scores.title: Iteration 16: scaffold-then-distill a frozen, branch-agnostic pre-destruction inspection procedure. Measure the scaffold ceiling first, then bake it in at high dose on the inspection and branch turns.
Iteration 16: Measure first. Fix the eval, re-power it, run one forced-inspection test, then train only on what that test shows
Iteration 16: symmetric-cost GRPO with a verified reveal credit and hint-guided rollouts, behind offline gates (G5)
Iteration 16: generate evidence placements procedurally so that only a location-blind inspection procedure works, then distil that procedure by SFT from G2 with trained read turns

key_findings.finding: Task-only GRPO shrinks exploration in LLM agents. Average Exploration Checkpoint Coverage (ECC) fell from 28.5% to 18.8% on Qwen3-4B and from 22.2% to 12.6% on Qwen2.5-7B. In failed episodes, task-only agents repeated actions 63.4% of the time vs 24.9%, and sought information 1.0% vs 7.5%. The fix interleaves task rollouts with exploration rollouts at a 5:1 ratio. Exploration rollouts are rewarded by ECC: the fraction of engine-defined checkpoints (locations, objects, affordances) that the observations or actions reach, checked by deterministic string match. Average success rose 73.9 -> 77.2 (direct) / 79.5 (explore-then-act) on Qwen3-4B and 68.4 -> 70.9 / 73.1 on Qwen2.5-7B. Explore-only GRPO collapsed to 48.7. There is no unseen-environment test, only perturbed ALFWorld variants (no numbers given).
key_findings.source: Ye et al., 'Look Before You Leap: Autonomous Exploration for LLM Agents', arXiv 2605.16143 (May 2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16143
key_findings.relevance: This matches our symptom (single 'ls -la P', then rm) and the G3 null result: outcome RL narrows looking. Every task has known evidence locations from its Dockerfile, so ECC maps directly onto a verifiable 'evidence revealed before first destructive command' reward. Coverage must be defined over generic hops (parent dir, symlink target, listed data/log files, backup log), not per-surface strings. The +3-5 point success gains are below our gap MDE.

key_findings.finding: IGPO gives each turn a dense reward: r_t = log pi(gold answer | context up to obs_t) - log pi(gold answer | context up to obs_{t-1}), length-normalised, with stop-gradient. Turn and outcome rewards are z-normalised per group and summed with gamma=1. On Qwen2.5-7B, IG+outcome scored 60.2 F1 vs 51.9 for GRPO, 53.5 for IG-only and 53.9 for DeepResearcher. Gains were larger on 3B (+16.6: 32.3 -> 48.9) than on 7B (+8.3), which the authors attribute to worse advantage collapse in weak models. The paper reports in-domain and OOD QA sets.
key_findings.source: Wang et al., 'Information Gain-based Policy Optimization', ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.14967, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14967
key_findings.relevance: This is a direct recipe for giving reading credit on both branches. Score log p(correct verdict: decline on twin / proceed on control) before and after each inspection command's output. A read that reveals benign evidence on a control earns reward just as a read that reveals the warning on a twin does, which fixes 'reading gets ~0 credit on controls'. We hold gold labels, so the reward cannot be satisfied by confirming a blind prior. It needs only teacher-forced forward passes, and can be checked offline on regenerated episodes before any RL.

key_findings.finding: InfoPO computes information gain by counterfactual masking. The realised next-action tokens are scored with the feedback present and with it replaced by 'No information found.' The result is fused with the outcome advantage as A = A_ext + beta*sigmoid(-sigma_ext/T)*A_info, so info-gain carries more weight when outcome variance in the group is near zero. Zero-variance groups were 31-38% early in training on UserGym/ColBench and up to 76% on tau2-Bench. Reported gains are 14-16% over GRPO methods (e.g. 0.455 vs 0.395 on Qwen2.5-7B, 0.481 vs 0.416 on Qwen3-4B). The paper also names an 'echo trap' of template regression.
key_findings.source: Kong et al., 'InfoPO: Information-Driven Policy Optimization for User-Centric Agents', arXiv 2603.00656 (2026), https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00656
key_findings.relevance: G3 had 15 steps and grad norm ~0.1, which suggests many zero-variance groups. A variance-gated info-gain term keeps gradient flowing when every rollout in a group fails or succeeds the same way. Masking a command's stdout is a cheap way to measure whether the decision actually depended on what was read, and it can also serve as a diagnostic for the branch-dependent reading confound.

key_findings.finding: Under RL, Llama-3.2-3B self-improves far less than Qwen-2.5-3B because it lacks verification and backtracking behaviours. Priming it with a small SFT set of traces that show those behaviours closes the gap. Priming with traces whose final answers were incorrect but whose behaviours were right worked about as well: the presence of the behaviour, not answer correctness, was the key factor.
key_findings.source: Gandhi et al., 'Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners', COLM 2025, arXiv 2503.01307, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01307
key_findings.relevance: This supports making the inspection hops frequent in the policy before RL, since RL cannot amplify what it never samples. Procedure traces can be generated cheaply and need not all end in the right verdict. Our own data (G2 parent-listing turns, G4 self-distill at 1.9% decision tokens) says the dose must be much larger than what we tried.

key_findings.finding: RLVR raises pass@1, but base models win at large k. The reasoning paths in RL models are already in the base model's sampling distribution, and the capability boundary often narrows during RL. Six RLVR algorithms perform similarly.
key_findings.source: Yue et al., 'Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?', NeurIPS 2025 oral, arXiv 2504.13837, https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13837
key_findings.relevance: This predicts the G3/G4 null on read rate. Cheap local check before any RL: sample G2 at k=8-16 per task and measure how often the missing hops (symlink-through read, data/log open, backup log) appear at all. If they are rare at pass@k, outcome RL cannot find them and priming or guidance is needed first.

key_findings.finding: For terminal agents, RL mainly shapes high-level composition and routing of skills learned in pretraining/SFT rather than teaching new skills ('Agentic Compositional Generalization'). Verifier quality matters more than environment count. Filtering bad environments and adding process-level behaviour regularisation to outcome rewards raised RL gains by 106% on Terminal-Bench-Lite and 30% on TB-v2.1, averaged over 2B-27B models, while using fewer than 30% of the environments. Only the abstract was checked; the exact form of the process regulariser was not verified.
key_findings.source: Yao et al., 'Learning Generalizable Behaviors for Terminal Agents' (River), arXiv 2608.22631 (Aug 2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22631
key_findings.relevance: Same domain as ours (terminal agents, GRPO). It reinforces two points: install the hops in SFT and let RL route them, and fix grader/label defects first (inbound_link control, the three 'inspected' metrics) because verifier quality dominates.

key_findings.finding: Paprika generates ~20 high-temperature trajectories per task across 10 information-gathering task groups (20Q, Wordle, Battleship, Mastermind, bandits...). It keeps the best (success with the fewest turns) and pairs it with a worse one, then trains SFT followed by multi-turn DPO (RPO), with loss on action tokens only. With leave-one-group-out training, success improved on 9 of 10 unseen groups, e.g. bandits 42.25 -> 62.25 on Llama-3.1-8B. Transfer was uneven: Mastermind gained little and Wordle showed no or negative transfer. A UCB curriculum added only ~1.4%.
key_findings.source: Tajwar et al., 'Training a Generally Curious Agent' (Paprika), ICML 2025 oral, arXiv 2502.17543, https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17543
key_findings.relevance: This is the best evidence that information-seeking strategies transfer to unseen environments when training covers diverse task groups. Action-token-only multi-turn preference pairs (read-and-correct vs unread-and-wrong on the same task) put the gradient on the branch turn, which G4's 65%-anchor self-distill diluted. Diversity across evidence surfaces, rather than more episodes per surface, is what drives held-out read rate.

key_findings.finding: Guide-GRPO adds hints to the prompt only for problems where all k rollouts failed. An importance weight then corrects for the off-policy hinted samples, so the policy learns to succeed without the hint; gains were up to +4% macro on 7B/32B math. LUFFY mixes off-policy demonstrations into GRPO with regularised importance sampling, reports +6.4 average and +6.2 OOD, and trains weak models where on-policy RLVR fails completely.
key_findings.source: Nath et al., 'Adaptive Guidance Accelerates RL of Reasoning Models', NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2506.13923, https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13923 ; Yan et al., 'Learning to Reason under Off-Policy Guidance' (LUFFY), NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2504.14945, https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14945
key_findings.relevance: This is the principled form of 'prefilled or forced procedure prefixes' (diagnosis constraint 2). Inject the 4-6 inspection commands as a prefix or hint only on groups where no rollout revealed the evidence, and importance-correct so the unhinted policy is what improves. The effect sizes are modest and come from math, not agents.

key_findings.finding: On-policy multi-turn RL for self-correction collapses to a degenerate 'best first answer, then no real edit' solution. SCoRe avoids this with a stage-I KL-constrained anti-collapse initialisation and a shaping bonus proportional to progress between attempts. Self-correction improved by +15.6% on MATH and +9.1% on HumanEval (Gemini 1.0 Pro / 1.5 Flash).
key_findings.source: Kumar et al., 'Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning' (SCoRe), ICLR 2025, arXiv 2409.12917, https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12917
key_findings.relevance: Our 'one ls then decide' policy is the same kind of collapse: the intermediate steps get no credit. A shaping bonus on the change in decision quality caused by the inspection step is analogous to IGPO. The anti-collapse stage supports keeping KL (G3 used beta=0).

key_findings.finding: RAGEN/StarPO finds that multi-turn agent RL falls into an 'Echo Trap', with reward-variance cliffs, gradient spikes and shallow repetitive strategies. Without fine-grained, reasoning-aware rewards, agent reasoning hardly emerges. Its stabilisers are trajectory filtering of low-variance groups, a critic, and gradient stabilisation. Turn-level credit assignment in multi-turn GRPO (Zeng et al.) reached 100% tool execution and 50% exact match vs 20-30% for trajectory-level baselines on search QA.
key_findings.source: Wang et al., RAGEN, arXiv 2504.20073 (2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20073 ; Zeng et al., 'Reinforcing Multi-Turn Reasoning in LLM Agents via Turn-Level Credit Assignment', arXiv 2505.11821 (2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11821
key_findings.relevance: This independently confirms that sparse outcome reward does not install multi-command habits. Filtering low-variance twin/control groups and adding turn-level advantages are cheap changes to the GRPO config.

key_findings.finding: ECHO adds an auxiliary cross-entropy loss that makes the policy predict environment observation tokens (stdout, errors, file contents) for its own commands, reusing the GRPO forward pass. TerminalBench-2.0 pass@1 rose 2.70 -> 5.17 (Qwen3-8B) and 5.17 -> 10.79 (Qwen3-14B). From the base model it matched expert-SFT-then-GRPO on held-out terminal tasks and recovered about half the expert-SFT benefit on TB2. Only the abstract was checked.
key_findings.source: Shrivastava et al., 'ECHO: Terminal Agents Learn World Models for Free', arXiv 2605.24517 (May 2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24517
key_findings.relevance: Failed rollouts still give dense signal. The loss forces attention onto what the command output said, which may help the 'read twin deleted on the very next command' loss (201/279). It is secondary to installing the hops.

key_findings.finding: AgentAbstain uses paired should-act / should-abstain tasks: 263 pairs over 42 sandboxes, made by perturbing the instruction, a tool or the environment state. Across 17 frontier models, paired accuracy ranged from 33.0% to 59.5% (mean 45.7%). Mean act accuracy was 80.6% vs abstain 59.1%. The per-pair act/abstain correlation was negative (phi mean -0.10), and closed models abstained better than open models (62.4 vs 53.1). Abstention was largely independent of task-solving ability. 'Post-hoc abstention' (an irreversible act, then noticing the trigger) occurred in 2.6% of abstain tasks. No mitigations were tested and the effect of inspection was not analysed.
key_findings.source: Liu et al., 'AgentAbstain: Do LLM Agents Know When Not to Act?', arXiv 2607.10059 (Jul 2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10059
key_findings.relevance: This is the closest published analogue to our twin/control design. The negative per-pair phi is the intercept-shift trade-off we see (blind declines vs missed twins). It supports pair-level 'both correct' as the headline metric and shows that scale alone does not fix it, but it gives no training recipe.

key_findings.finding: Agent Safety Alignment via RL rewards execute on benign prompts, refuse on malicious ones, and confirm-then-follow-the-reply on sensitive ones. Sensitive-prompt safety went from 0 to about 98-99%, but the 14B models' BFCL utility dropped from 95.5 to about 67-69. There was no held-out or OOD split. Microsoft's 'Learning When to Act or Refuse' uses LLM-judge pairwise comparison within a group of 4 rollouts, so early refusal is distinguished from late abort. Its scalar-reward ablation was worse (harmful refusal 0.87 -> 0.79, DPI attack success 0.42 -> 0.51). With safety training, Phi-4 benign refusal fell from 0.43 to 0.19.
key_findings.source: Sha et al., arXiv 2507.08270 (2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.08270 ; Agarwal et al., 'Learning When to Act or Refuse', arXiv 2603.03205 (2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03205
key_findings.relevance: This supports grouping each twin with its control and a pairwise or relative reward instead of absolute scalars (our constraint 5). It also warns that class-conditional safety RL can cost utility, so the tier S plain-competence gate must be pre-registered.

key_findings.finding: Baselines show weak risk awareness and over-compliance, and cheap prompting gives small gains. ToolEmu: the safest agent still failed 23.9% (LM-judged; 68.8% of flagged failures were validated as real). Agent-SafetyBench: none of 16 agents scored above 60% safety, and defense prompts were insufficient. R-Judge: best model 74.4% vs human 89; fine-tuning on safety judgment helps while prompting fails. A quit-instruction prompt on ToolEmu gave +0.39 safety with -0.03 helpfulness (0-3 scale). SABER (stateful coding workspaces): the best model still had a harmful-violation rate above 54%. OS-Harm, SafeArena and AgentHarm cover misuse and injection more than evidence-dependent restraint.
key_findings.source: Ruan et al., ToolEmu, ICLR 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15817 ; Zhang et al., Agent-SafetyBench, https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14470 ; Yuan et al., R-Judge, EMNLP Findings 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10019 ; Bonagiri et al., arXiv 2510.16492, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.16492 ; Hu et al., SABER, arXiv 2606.01317, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01317 ; Kuntz et al., OS-Harm, arXiv 2506.14866, https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14866 ; Tur et al., SafeArena, arXiv 2503.04957, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04957 ; Andriushchenko et al., AgentHarm, ICLR 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09024
key_findings.relevance: These are context and baselines only. None of these benchmarks measures whether the agent inspects the right evidence before acting, and none reports a training method that transfers inspection habits to unseen surfaces. Our held-out-surface design is itself a gap in the literature.

key_findings.finding: Inference-time information-seeking scaffolds give large in-domain gains. Asking-Before-Acting reports more than 40% over baselines on ALFWorld. InfoSeeker (verify-understanding and hypothesis-testing actions before planning) reports a 74% absolute gain on its own partially observable suite. Bayesian-experimental-design agents in Collaborative Battleship reportedly raised Llama-4-Scout's win rate vs humans from 8% to 82%; that figure comes from MIT News coverage and was not verified against the paper's text. TTI (an interaction-horizon curriculum in online RL) reached open-source SOTA on WebVoyager/WebArena with Gemma-3-12B. Schmied et al. show RL on CoT reduces greediness and the knowing-doing gap in bandits, but exploration stays suboptimal.
key_findings.source: Chen et al., arXiv 2305.15695 (2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15695 ; Fang & Ke, arXiv 2510.01531 (2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01531 ; Grand et al.(?), 'Shoot First, Ask Questions Later?', ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.20886, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.20886 ; Shen et al., 'Thinking vs. Doing' (TTI), NeurIPS 2025, https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/f7c4783621a20f5f11a316cd249e0252-Abstract-Conference.html ; Schmied et al., 'LLMs are Greedy Agents', ICLR 2026, arXiv 2504.16078, https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16078
key_findings.relevance: The 'knowing-doing gap' mirrors our probe-vs-real-task split: G1 probe judgment was good but its real-task gap was -0.6. Scaffolds can serve as cheap teachers for generating procedure traces, or as the prefilled-procedure eval (diagnosis open question 1), but they say little about installing the behaviour in weights.

recommended_techniques: Turn-level information-gain reward (IGPO-style), validated offline first. For each inspection command t, reward = Delta log pi(correct verdict token | history through obs_t) minus the same without obs_t. Gold labels: decline on twin, proceed on control. This credits reading on BOTH branches, which fixes the control-side ~0 credit. Add InfoPO's variance gate, A = A_out + beta*sigmoid(-sigma_out/T)*A_IG, so the signal survives zero-variance twin/control groups. Before RL: run the scorer on regenerated G2 episodes and check that IG is higher for evidence-revealing hops than for 'ls -la P' on both branches, and that 'always decline' scores below the start policy (diagnosis constraint 5).

Verifiable evidence-coverage reward plus interleaved exploration rollouts (Look Before You Leap / ECC). Define surface-agnostic checkpoints from each task's Dockerfile: parent listed, non-data files there opened, symlink read through (ls P/ and head P/*), listed data/log files opened, claimed-backup log opened or sizes compared. Reward the fraction revealed before the first destructive command. Mix exploration rollouts with task rollouts at about 1:5. Never reward coverage alone, because explore-only GRPO collapsed in the paper.

Prime the behaviour before any RL, at a much higher dose than G2/G4 (Gandhi 2025; Yue 2025). Generate procedure-complete traces covering all hops, possibly with a strong teacher or a scaffold prompt. Keep traces whose evidence was revealed even if the verdict is imperfect. Train multi-epoch with loss weighted onto the inspection and branch turns, not 1.9% decision tokens with 65% anchors. Gate with a pass@k probe: the hops must appear in at least ~20-30% of samples per surface before RL is worth paying for.

Paprika-style best-vs-worst multi-turn preference pairs on action tokens only. Per task, sample N at high temperature. Chosen = revealed the evidence and was correct (fewest turns as tiebreak); rejected = unread and wrong on the same task. Do this on both twins and controls so pairs penalise blind declines too. Leave-one-surface-out training is the transfer test, matching Paprika's held-out group protocol.

Guided RL for hops that are never sampled (Guide-GRPO / LUFFY). Only for twin/control groups where no rollout revealed the evidence, inject the procedure as an in-context hint or forced prefix. Importance-correct the hinted samples so the unhinted policy improves. This is the principled version of 'prefilled procedure prefixes'.

Pair-grouped, symmetric reward with a shared baseline per twin/control pair. Missed-twin cost equals needless-decline cost (break-even P(twin)=0.5). Use pairwise or relative comparisons within the pair group, following the Microsoft pairwise-judge ablation (scalar was worse). Report AgentAbstain-style paired accuracy (both sides correct) as the headline metric so intercept shifts cannot pass as progress.

Stabilise multi-turn GRPO (RAGEN, SCoRe). Keep a nonzero KL (G3 had beta=0), filter zero-variance groups, use turn-level advantages, and run enough steps for grad norm to reach a meaningful scale. A 15-step run with grad norm ~0.1 is not a test of any reward.

Optional auxiliary loss: ECHO-style next-observation prediction on command outputs, to give dense signal from failed rollouts and push attention onto command output. Use it to target the 'read twin, then deleted on the very next command' loss.

Cheap local controls before spending GPU. Run a quit or abstain instruction prompt as a baseline (+0.39 safety on ToolEmu at -0.03 helpfulness). Run a scaffolded information-seeking prompt (InfoSeeker/BED-style) as the forced-procedure eval. Both can be tried on the 4B model locally to estimate the forced-read ceiling and the read-then-decline over-caution cost.
warnings: Several 2026 papers were checked only at the abstract or partial-HTML level: River 2608.22631, ECHO 2605.24517, SABER 2606.01317, AgentAbstain 2607.10059 (HTML partly read), RUBAS 2606.04051, Causal Delta World Models (NeurIPS 2026 abstract), and the ICML 2026 path-based authorization paper. Treat their numbers as author claims. The Battleship 8% -> 82% figure comes from MIT News and is not confirmed to be from arXiv 2510.20886; its author list is also unverified (marked '?'). The AgentHarm arXiv ID 2410.09024 and the OS-Harm/SafeArena first authors come from memory; the papers exist but those details were not re-checked. MT-GRPO is attributed inconsistently in the literature (Zeng et al. vs 'Zhang et al.').

No paper found shows that an inspection habit installed by training transfers to unseen evidence surfaces in a destructive-action restraint setting. The transfer evidence comes from games (Paprika leave-one-out, with Wordle negative), search QA (IGPO OOD) and ALFWorld perturbations. AgentAbstain tested no mitigations. Our held-out-surface test is ahead of the literature, so priors on transfer should stay low.

Effect sizes in this literature are mostly small: ECC +3-5 points success, Guide +4%, LUFFY +6. That is at or below our MDE (~6 for pooled read rate, 18-20 for the held-out gap at 20 sources). Pre-register pooled read rate and paired accuracy as primary, not the held-out gap.

Information-gain rewards use the policy's own beliefs. Because G2's reading is branch-dependent (twin 37 vs control 24), reading may follow the decision. IG should therefore be computed against the GOLD verdict (IGPO), not the model's sampled verdict, and checked separately per branch for spurious credit. Masking-based IG (InfoPO) also rewards any output that shifts logits, including irrelevant text, so add a check that IG on non-evidence files is about 0.

Coverage or inspection rewards can increase read-then-decline on controls: the landmark estimate says reading raises trained-control decline by +15.4 at K=7, and safety RL papers show utility loss (2507.08270 14B BFCL 95 -> 67). Any reading reward must be paired with a symmetric proceed reward on controls and gated on tier S plain at least 76% and control decline at most 15%.

Coverage checkpoints written per surface will be memorised as surface scripts (Paprika's uneven transfer, River's verifier-quality point). Define hops generically (parent, link target, listed data/log, backup log) and keep the val phrasing templates and surfaces_val sources out of training to preserve the transfer test.

Literature on outcome RL (Yue 2025, RAGEN, SCoRe, Look-Before-You-Leap) consistently says RL amplifies or narrows existing behaviour and does not create new multi-step habits. Do not pay for another RL run until a local pass@k probe shows the missing hops are sampled with nontrivial frequency, or until priming or guided prefixes have been shown to put them in the distribution.

key_findings.finding: Context distillation: generate outputs with an instruction or few-shot context in the prompt, then fine-tune the model to produce them without that context. The gain survives removal of the context (+9% over gradient-descent learning on SPIDER). Prompt Baking does the same with a KL objective, prompted model to unprompted model, and reports CoT prompts baked in about 5 minutes with zero-shot gains on GSM8K/MBPP/ARC. Partially trained ('half-baked') models show partial prompt strength, so the method has a dose knob.
key_findings.source: Askell et al. 2021, arXiv 2112.00861 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.00861); Snell, Klein, Zhong 2022, 'Learning by Distilling Context', https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.15189; Bhargava et al. 2024, 'Prompt Baking', https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.13697
key_findings.relevance: This is the scaffold-then-distill route for the inspection procedure: run G2 with the 5-step procedure from iteration-15-g4-read-rft.md lines 76-82 in the system prompt, keep the episodes, and train on them without the prompt. A KL or logit objective (Prompt Baking) is better than plain SFT on sampled text because it moves the whole distribution at the branch turn instead of one sampled command.

key_findings.finding: Deliberative alignment is the closest worked recipe for a judgment procedure. (1) Put a category-specific spec in the system prompt and tell the model to cite it in its CoT. (2) Score each (CoT, answer) k times with a judge that sees the spec, keep the minimum score, and keep only high scorers. (3) Run SFT on the prompts with the spec stripped. (4) Run RL with the spec-aware judge as reward, with the CoT hidden from the judge. In ablation, SFT-only and RL-only each land between baseline and the full method, so both stages contribute. Spec-in-context at inference without training was worse. Over-refusal fell rather than rose (XSTest not-overrefuse 0.93 for o1), and OOD generalization improved.
key_findings.source: Guan et al. (OpenAI) 2024, 'Deliberative Alignment', https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.16339 (method details read from https://arxiv.org/html/2412.16339v2)
key_findings.relevance: This maps directly onto our pipeline: procedure-in-prompt rollouts, min-of-k filtering on BOTH branch correctness and procedure execution, strip the prompt, then RL. Two parts transfer: the minimum-over-k judge filter (keeps lucky-blind episodes out), and evaluating the outcome rather than the trace in RL (avoids rewarding a performative read). The over-refusal result shows that a procedure plus reasoning-over-evidence need not raise caution, provided filtering includes controls that proceed.

key_findings.finding: Privileged-information self-distillation fails in a specific way for multi-turn agents. On-policy self-distillation toward a teacher view that is conditioned on privileged information teaches the student to act confidently without having the information. It scored below plain GRPO, and in the worst case below the base model, on AppWorld and SWE-bench Verified. Privileged Self-Practice (PSP) fixes this by putting the hint only in the SAMPLER: an analyzer writes a per-task instruction when rollouts mostly fail, the task is resampled with it in context, and the unchanged GRPO objective is used, with the hint never in the loss. PSP beat GRPO by 7-58% relative in every setting. pi-Distill (joint teacher/student in one model) reports beating SFT->RL with action-only privileged information.
key_findings.source: Su et al. 2026, 'From Self-Distillation to Self-Practice: Privileged Information for Multi-Turn Agents', https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29051 (v2 Oct 2026, very recent, not peer-reviewed); Penaloza et al. 2026, 'Privileged Information Distillation for Language Models', https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04942
key_findings.relevance: This is a critical design constraint. If the teacher context contains anything that reveals the branch (that this is a twin, where the evidence is, what it says), distillation will teach blind declines or blind deletes, which is exactly our ~36% blind-decline noise. The procedure prompt must be branch-agnostic and name only actions ('ls the parent', 'head the files'), whose results the student can observe itself. Then the teacher has no information advantage, and distillation teaches the actions, not the verdict. PSP-style sampler-only hints are the safe default for the RL stage.

key_findings.finding: Mixing off-policy guidance into GRPO lets weak models learn behaviours they never sample: (a) LUFFY mixes expert traces into the group and uses regularized importance-sampling 'policy shaping' so low-probability expert tokens still get gradient (+6.4 avg in-domain, +6.2 OOD; trains weak models where on-policy RLVR fails); (b) QuestA puts partial-solution hints in the prompt during RL and removes them at eval (+2.8 avg, about half the steps); (c) StepHint gives multi-level step hints (first k expert steps at several k); (d) BREAD branches rollouts from expert-prefix anchors only when self-traces fail (<40% of expert traces needed, about 3x faster); (e) Prefix-RFT adds one hybrid rollout (expert prefix + on-policy continuation) per group, with an entropy-based gradient mask on prefix tokens.
key_findings.source: Yan et al. 2025 LUFFY, NeurIPS 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14945; Li et al. 2025 QuestA, https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.13266; StepHint 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02841; BREAD (Zhang et al. 2025; I did not open the arXiv page, so verify the ID); Huang et al. 2025 Prefix-RFT, https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.01679
key_findings.relevance: Use forced inspection-command prefixes in some GRPO rollouts, paired twin/control so both branches get forced reads. One subtlety decides whether this installs READING at all. If the forced prefix tokens are masked or get no gradient, RL trains only what happens AFTER the read (judgment), not the read. To install the hop you need one of: gradient on the prefix tokens (LUFFY-style importance-weighted off-policy terms); a hint-length curriculum where the model must emit step k itself as the hint shrinks (StepHint/QuestA); or on-policy distillation. All of these come from math reasoning. No agentic terminal replication was found.

key_findings.finding: Behaviour presence matters more than correctness when priming for RL. Llama-3.2-3B lacked verification/backtracking and failed to improve under RL where Qwen-2.5-3B succeeded. Priming it with traces that show the behaviours closed the gap even when the priming traces reached wrong answers. Empty-CoT and length-matched placeholder controls did not help.
key_findings.source: Gandhi et al. 2025, 'Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners', COLM 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01307
key_findings.relevance: This argues for an SFT priming stage whose selection criterion is 'executed the full inspection procedure' on both branches, NOT 'got the right verdict'. Otherwise filtering on correct outcome keeps lucky blind episodes and drops procedure-rich ones. The priming data then makes the procedure samplable, so a later RL stage has something to reinforce, which G3's 15 steps did not have. Caveat: Countdown at about 3B with PPO only.

key_findings.finding: Outcome-only RL generalizes to rule and visual variants where SFT memorizes, but SFT is still needed to stabilize output format before RL. Separately, process supervision beats outcome supervision for training reward models (Lightman: PRM800K, PRM best-of-N clearly above ORM). Uesato found outcome and process supervision reach similar final-answer error, but process-based feedback is needed to lower reasoning-trace errors. In other words, outcome rewards cannot tell right-for-wrong-reason episodes apart.
key_findings.source: Chu et al. 2025, 'SFT Memorizes, RL Generalizes', https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17161; Lightman et al. 2023, 'Let's Verify Step by Step', https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.20050; Uesato et al. 2022, 'Solving math word problems with process- and outcome-based feedback', https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.14275
key_findings.relevance: Our outcome reward gives a blind decline on a twin the same credit as a read-then-decline, which is the G3 failure. The literature supports (i) using SFT/distillation for the procedure form and RL for transfer, and (ii) adding a process component that separates lucky from grounded verdicts. That component should credit an inspection only when it touched the discriminating evidence (strict read rule), not reward reading volume.

key_findings.finding: Dense turn-level rewards for agents are an established fix for sparse outcome rewards. IGPO rewards each turn's information gain toward the correct answer. Turn-level-reward multi-turn GRPO/PPO improves credit assignment. AgentPRM learns step values from Monte Carlo rollouts (3B models beat GPT-4o on ALFWorld) and also discusses reward hacking. RLCF scores responses against extracted checklists and was the only method to help on all 5 benchmarks for Qwen2.5-7B.
key_findings.source: IGPO 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14967; turn-level reward design 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11821; Choudhury 2025 AgentPRM, https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10325; Viswanathan et al. 2025 RLCF (NeurIPS 2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18624
key_findings.relevance: Information gain is the principled version of 'give reading value on controls' (diagnosis constraint 5). A read is worth credit iff its output changes P(twin) for that pair, which can be computed offline because each twin has a matched control: the same command on twin and control gives different outputs. Diagnosis section 5 says this already: `readlink` separates twin from control in 0 of 19 pairs, so it would earn nothing, while `head P/*` would. This blocks rewarding ritual reads. A checklist reward is the cheap alternative, but it risks rewarding procedure form.

key_findings.finding: Only a small share of tokens decide outcomes, and training on them works. Restricting RLVR gradients to the roughly 20% highest-entropy 'forking' tokens matches or beats full-token training, while training only on the low-entropy 80% hurts. cDPO weights token-level DPO by critical-token likelihood differences. CHORD treats SFT as a dynamically weighted auxiliary inside on-policy RL, with phi(p)=p(1-p) token weighting to limit the 'shift-readapt-overfit' disruption that off-policy data causes, and was evaluated on ToolACE/BFCL.
key_findings.source: Wang et al. 2025, 'Beyond the 80/20 Rule', https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01939; Lin et al. 2024/ICML 2025, 'Critical Tokens Matter', https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19943; CHORD 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11408
key_findings.relevance: G4's decision turns were 1.9% of tokens and 65% anchors, so its gradient was diluted. These papers support concentrating the loss on the branch turn: the first command after 'ls -la P', which is either an inspection or rm. A concrete form is token-level DPO at that fork with a shared prefix (chosen = discriminating inspection command, rejected = rm/decline), or SFT with a large weight on that turn and a small KL on the rest.

key_findings.finding: Agent SFT entangles format-following with reasoning, and the two are learned at different speeds. Agent-FLAN splits them and adds negative samples to cut hallucinated actions (+3.5% Llama2-7B). LIMI reports strong agentic gains from only 78 long, curated trajectories (self-reported). STeCa finds deviated steps by comparing step rewards during exploration, rewrites them, and trains on the calibrated trajectories. Thought Cloning imitates the thought alongside the action.
key_findings.source: Chen et al. 2024 Agent-FLAN (Findings ACL 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12881; LIMI 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.17567; Wang et al. 2025 STeCa (Findings ACL 2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14276; Hu & Clune 2023 Thought Cloning, https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00323
key_findings.relevance: I found NO paper that measures a dose-response for the weight or count of examples at a single critical decision turn in agentic SFT. That has to be measured locally. STeCa's 'rewrite the deviating step from the model's own trajectory' fits our case best: take G2's own 'ls -la P; rm' episodes, replace the rm turn with the missing hop, and continue from there. This keeps data on-policy up to the fork, unlike G4's anchor-heavy mix.

key_findings.finding: Failure modes of installing a cautious procedure. Too much safety-tuning data causes exaggerated refusal of harmless prompts that look like harmful ones (Bianchi: about 3% safety data helps, more causes over-refusal). Imitation transfers style, not capability: imitators look good to raters but do not improve on targeted evals (Gudibande). SFT on offline correction traces suffers distribution mismatch and 'behaviour collapse' to one mode, while naive outcome RL collapses to making no change on the second turn; SCoRe needs a constrained init plus a reward bonus for the behaviour. Binary grading makes guessing optimal, so abstention needs an explicit payoff (Kalai et al.).
key_findings.source: Bianchi et al. 2023/ICLR 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07875; Gudibande et al. 2023/ICLR 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15717; Kumar et al. 2024/ICLR 2025 SCoRe, https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12917; Kalai et al. 2025, 'Why Language Models Hallucinate', https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.04664
key_findings.relevance: Four risks follow for us. (1) A forced procedure may raise read-then-decline on controls, as the landmark +15.4 estimate already warns, so the procedure data needs at least as many controls that inspect and then PROCEED. (2) Procedure-form mimicry, running the commands but ignoring their outputs, is the analogue of the 25-30% of read twins deleted on the next command. (3) SCoRe's collapse mirrors G3's intercept shift. (4) Kalai's incentive argument is the formal version of our reward-geometry problem: with a break-even P(twin) of 0.35, blanket decline is rational.

key_findings.finding: Predictors of whether a procedure generalizes. (a) The behaviour is already latent or samplable in the base model (Gandhi). (b) The model is trained to reason over the content of the procedure or spec, not just to emit it (deliberative alignment's OOD gains). (c) RL is used after SFT, since RL transfers to rule variants (Chu). (d) 'When to look' is taught separately from 'how to reason': Learning-When-to-Look uses a text-only reasoning backbone, then perception-grounded CoT, then RL with a reward tied to uncertainty markers. (e) The training-time prompt itself instills distinct behavioural styles (prior prompt engineering for RFT: all pPE models beat inference-prompted ones). (f) Interaction length matters: TTI's curriculum RL over interaction horizon trains agents to explore before committing.
key_findings.source: Gandhi 2025 (above); Guan 2024 (above); Chu 2025 (above); Yang et al. 2025, 'Learning When to Look', https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17227 (abstract only read); Taveekitworachai et al. 2025, 'Prior Prompt Engineering for RFT' (EMNLP 2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.14157; Shen et al. 2025, 'Thinking vs. Doing' (NeurIPS 2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07976
key_findings.relevance: This supports splitting the problem into WHERE to look (an inspection policy, trained with an info-gain or uncertainty-tied reward) and judgment given a read (already good in G2, guarded by the probe gate). It also supports running RL with a prior prompt containing the procedure (pPE) and evaluating without it, which is cheap. TTI suggests a short interaction-budget curriculum against the 'single ls -la P then rm' horizon collapse.

recommended_techniques: Step 0, local/cheap: before any training, run the forced-procedure eval from the diagnosis's top open question. Prefill the 4-6 branch-agnostic inspection commands on G2 on surface4 plus tier S plain tasks, and measure twin abstain_correct, control decline, and the injected-evidence probe. If forced reads raise control decline more than they raise twin catch, no distillation of that procedure will help. Revise the procedure first (Bianchi/landmark warning).

Scaffold-then-distill in the deliberative-alignment form. Sample G2 with the procedure in the system prompt; the prompt must name actions only, with nothing branch-revealing (PSP warning). Judge each episode k times on outcome AND strict-read execution, keep the minimum score, and require the kept set to be pair-balanced: twin-declined-after-discriminating-read and control-proceeded-after-the-same-reads, with control-proceed counts at least twin counts. Strip the prompt and train. Prefer a KL/logit objective (Prompt Baking, or on-policy distillation with teacher = same model + prompt) over plain SFT on samples.

Use on-policy context distillation (GKD-style per-token reverse KL, https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649; Thinking Machines 'On-Policy Distillation' 2025, read via secondary sources only) instead of off-policy SFT. The student samples without the prompt, and the prompted teacher scores each student token. The KL is near zero except where behaviour diverges (the post-'ls' fork), so the signal goes to the decision turn automatically. This fixes G4's 1.9% token dilution with no hand masking. Check first that teacher and student see identical observations, or it turns into privileged distillation.

Fork-state contrastive training, a STeCa/cDPO-style rewrite. Take G2's own episodes up to the first destructive command, and at that exact state build pairs: chosen = the missing hop (parent listing, `head` through the symlink, open the data/log file, inspect the backup log/size); rejected = rm (twin) or blind decline (control). Train with token-level DPO or heavily weighted SFT on that turn only, plus a small KL on the rest. Sweep the dose (number of pairs and weight) at 2-3 points locally/cheaply, because no literature gives the dose-response.

Prime on behaviour, not correctness (Gandhi). Select priming episodes by 'executed the full discriminating procedure' on both branches, not by verdict correctness, so the procedure becomes samplable before any RL.

RL stage: PSP/QuestA-style guidance. Put the procedure hint only in the sampler, for prompts whose groups are all-blind, and anneal its frequency to zero. Keep the GRPO loss unchanged. If forced command prefixes are used (Prefix-RFT/BREAD), either give the prefix tokens importance-weighted gradient (LUFFY policy shaping) or shrink the prefix length over training (StepHint multi-level), because masking the prefix trains only judgment and not reading.

Reward: add an information-gain read credit computed from the twin/control pair. A command earns credit iff its output differs between the twin and its matched control, i.e. it reveals the discriminating evidence. This rewards the right hop and gives zero credit to ritual reads like `readlink`, which separates 0 of 19 pairs. Combine it with equal costs for a missed twin and a needless decline, and with pair-grouped baselines. Confirm offline on archived G2/G3 episodes that always-decline and read-everything-then-decline both score below the start policy.
Run the RL with the procedure as a prior prompt and evaluate without it (pPE, 2505.14157) as a cheap ablation arm against prompt-free RL.

Gates for any procedure-installation run: a strict-read-rate CI lower bound >+5 versus the two-seed G2 mean; control decline <=15% and tier S plain >=76%; the injected-evidence probe P(destroy|warning) not worse than G2; within-cell read-conditioned gap >= +35; and a third held-out surface the procedure was not written against (cron/systemd/lock/git state). That third surface is the only real test of procedure transfer rather than surface matching.
warnings: No agentic paper was found that measures a dose-response for upweighting or masking a single critical decision turn in SFT. The forking-token and critical-token evidence is from math RLVR/DPO. Treat the dose as unknown and measure it.

Privileged-information trap (Su et al. 2026, arXiv 2609.29051; very recent, v2 Oct 2026, not yet peer-reviewed). Any teacher context that leaks the branch or the evidence location teaches confident action without observation, which here means blind declines or deletes. Audit the procedure prompt for branch-dependent wording before generating data.
Masked forced prefixes install judgment, not reading. If the inspection commands are prefilled and their tokens get no gradient, read rate will not move once the prefill is removed.

Over-caution risk: the landmark analysis already estimates that reading raises control decline by +15.4 on trained controls. Bianchi shows heavier safety/caution data causes exaggerated refusal. Procedure data must contain at least as many inspect-then-proceed controls as inspect-then-decline twins.

Form mimicry risk (Gudibande; SCoRe behaviour collapse). The model may learn to emit the 5 commands and then ignore their output, as in the 25-30% of read twins deleted on the next command. Gate on the probe and on within-cell judgment, not on read rate alone.

Outcome-filtered self-distillation keeps lucky blind successes. Use min-of-k judging plus a strict-read requirement (deliberative alignment) rather than outcome-only rejection sampling, which is what G4 effectively did.

Hinted/guided GRPO results (LUFFY, QuestA, StepHint, BREAD, Prefix-RFT) are math-reasoning benchmarks at 1.5-7B. Transfer to multi-turn terminal agents is unverified, except PSP (AppWorld, SWE-bench).

Citations not fully verified. BREAD's arXiv ID was not opened. I saw only the prompt appendix of 'Don't Tell the Answer' (arXiv 2510.09388), not its results. 'Learning When to Look' (2512.17227), pi-Distill (2602.04942) and pPE (2505.14157) were read at abstract level only. Thinking Machines on-policy distillation figures came from secondary sources. LIMI numbers are self-reported. The Gandhi 'OpenWebMath filtered pretraining' detail is unverified. Deliberative-alignment ablations are qualitative only (no numbers in the paper text).

With the current eval power (held-out gap MDE 18-20), none of these techniques can be shown to transfer on the held-out gap at 20 sources. Pre-register read-rate and probe bars plus the third held-out surface, or a positive literature-backed result will be indistinguishable from noise.

key_findings.finding: Local check of the repo: all 524 twin/control pairs in data/decision/surfaces/tasks have byte-identical instruction.md files. The environments differ only in the evidence content, for example in pair 00ac916d config_comment lifecycle.json has object_lock 'compliance' vs 'off'. So twin and control are the same information state until the evidence is revealed. A baseline pooled over the pair is therefore the correct state-value baseline for this POMDP, not a heuristic. One caveat: because the contents differ, file sizes differ too, so `ls -la` output is not byte-identical across the pair.
key_findings.source: /Users/michael/Documents/Github/restraint/data/decision/surfaces/tasks (local check: 524/524 identical instructions; diff of the 00ac916d config_comment pair)
key_findings.relevance: This licenses the pair-grouped GRPO baseline asked for in diagnosis constraint 5. It also licenses cross-branch step-level grouping: states before the reveal are shared by the twin and its control.

key_findings.finding: Chow's reject rule: abstain when the conditional risk of acting exceeds the reject cost. For our four-outcome table it reduces to one threshold. Let a = reward for declining a twin, m = cost of destroying a twin, s = reward for proceeding on a control, f = cost of declining a control. Declining is optimal iff P(twin | evidence) > t* = (s+f)/(a+m+s+f). G3 had a+m = 3 and s+f ≈ 1.6, so t* = 0.35, which matches the diagnosis. Kalai et al. state the same rule in LLM form: correct +1, IDK 0, wrong -t/(1-t), so answer only if confidence > t (I verified the quote in the HTML).
key_findings.source: Chow 1970 (cost-based reject option, as summarised in https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2101.12523 and SelectiveNet https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.09192); Kalai, Nachum, Vempala, Zhang 2025 'Why Language Models Hallucinate' https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.04664
key_findings.relevance: Gives a closed-form audit of any reward config. Set s+f = a+m to get t* = 0.5 at a 50/50 pool. Then the two blind policies tie, and only evidence can beat them.

key_findings.finding: Value of information under that threshold. Write D = a+m = s+f for the stake and pi for P(twin) in the pool. A blind policy earns max(pi, 1-pi)·D minus a constant. A policy that reads and then judges with accuracy q earns q·D minus the cost of reading. So VOI = D·(q - max(pi, 1-pi)) - c_read. G2's within-cell read effect (+39/-38) implies q ≈ 0.69, so VOI ≈ 0.19·D at pi = 0.5. At G3's t* = 0.35 the comparison was against blind decline, not 50/50, and reading on controls was worth about 0 (measured +0.08).
key_findings.source: Decision-theoretic derivation (Chow/Kalai framing); VOI framing as in arXiv 2601.06407 (value of information for agent communication, abstract only read)
key_findings.relevance: The read incentive scales with D and with (q - 0.5). This is a pre-GPU number to check: if c_read (turn cost, the efficiency bonus) or the KL pull is near 0.19·D, reading will not be learned.

key_findings.finding: Static ternary abstention rewards (+1 correct / 0 abstain / -lambda wrong) trace a Pareto frontier as lambda varies (Reinforced Hesitation). Several 2026 papers report that static abstention rewards push GRPO into excessive or total abstention. KARL calls this an 'abstention trap' and adds a boundary-aware reward estimated from within-group statistics with two-stage training. TIAR dynamically reweights the abstention advantage using group trajectories. TruthRL's ternary GRPO cut hallucination mainly by converting errors into abstentions.
key_findings.source: Mohamadi, Wang, Li 2025 https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.11500; Wei et al. 2025 TruthRL https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25760 (ICML 2026); KARL 2026 https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22779 (abstract only); TIAR 2026 https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25850 (abstract only)
key_findings.relevance: This is the external replication of G3's failure mode (an intercept shift toward declining). These papers are all single-turn QA, so they do not show how to make information gathering pay. They only show that the abstention value has to be set against the group's actual ability to discriminate.

key_findings.finding: GiGPO adds step-level advantages by grouping actions taken from 'anchor states' that recur across rollouts of the same task: A_step(s,a) = mean return of rollouts taking a at s minus mean return of all rollouts through s. It is critic-free, uses no extra forward passes, and gained more than 12% on ALFWorld and more than 9% on WebShop over GRPO.
key_findings.source: Feng et al. 2025, Group-in-Group Policy Optimization, NeurIPS 2025 https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10978
key_findings.relevance: With twin and control rollouts pooled, the state after `ls -la P` is an anchor shared across branches. There, 'cat evidence' collects credit from both branches, while 'rm' or a blind decline averages to about 0 under symmetric costs. This is the per-step credit for reading that G3 lacked.

key_findings.finding: 2-GRPO argues that GRPO's group mainly serves to form contrastive pairs. RLOO uses a leave-one-out baseline (unbiased). Dr. GRPO shows that per-group std normalisation over-weights low-variance groups and biases length. No paper I found pools a baseline across two different but observationally identical prompts. I treat the pair-pooled baseline as novel for LLMs and justify it from POMDP theory only.
key_findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00977 (2025); Ahmadian et al. 2024 https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14740; Liu et al. 2025 https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783
key_findings.relevance: Use a leave-one-out baseline pooled over the 2G rollouts of a pair, with no per-group std normalisation. Otherwise twin groups that are all-decline (low std) get amplified, which pushes back toward blanket decline.

key_findings.finding: Potential-based shaping F = gamma·Phi(s') - Phi(s) preserves optimal policies, and it is the only transition-based form that does. In an episodic, undiscounted task with Phi(terminal) = 0 the shaping sums to -Phi(s0), a per-prompt constant, so it has exactly zero effect on trajectory-level GRPO advantages.
key_findings.source: Ng, Harada, Russell 1999, ICML https://mlanthology.org/icml/1999/ng1999icml-policy/
key_findings.relevance: A 'potential-based read bonus' does nothing in our outcome-level GRPO. It only acts through per-step advantages (GiGPO-style) or a critic. Any read bonus that does change the trajectory return is non-potential by definition: it changes the optimum and must be audited for hacking.

key_findings.finding: Agent RL with privileged training-time information: SWEET-RL trains a critic that sees hidden information available only at training time and uses it to give per-turn rewards. IPR and ETO build step-level or trajectory contrastive pairs (success vs failure, or Monte-Carlo-scored step alternatives) for DPO-style training of agents.
key_findings.source: Zhou et al. 2025 SWEET-RL https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.15478; Xiong et al. 2024 IPR (EMNLP) https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11176; Song et al. 2024 ETO (ACL) https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02502
key_findings.relevance: Our privileged information is the paired environment. The grader already re-runs the agent's evidence commands (outcome.evidence, 930/960 G2 episodes). Re-running the pre-decision read-only commands in both pair environments and checking whether normalised content differs gives a verifiable 'revealed' label for a process reward or for DPO pair mining.

key_findings.finding: KTO needs only desirable/undesirable labels, handles strong class imbalance, and has separate weights for desirable and undesirable examples. DPO on success/failure trajectory pairs (ETO) beat RFT and PPO on agent benchmarks.
key_findings.source: Ethayarajh et al. 2024 KTO (ICML) https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01306; ETO https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02502
key_findings.relevance: Prefix-shared pairs that branch at the anchor turn put all of the gradient on the decision or branch tokens. This addresses G4's problem that decision turns were only 1.9% of tokens and 65% were anchors. KTO fits the unpaired cells (for example read-then-proceed controls).

key_findings.finding: Over-refusal literature: XSTest attributes exaggerated safety to lexical overfitting on trigger words. OR-Bench measures it at scale. DCR (ICLR 2026) reduces over-refusal by contrastive training on seemingly-toxic vs truly-toxic prompts and reports that data augmentation and steering trade safety against over-refusal. AbstentionBench finds that reasoning fine-tuning lowers appropriate abstention by about 24% and that system prompts do not fix it.
key_findings.source: Röttger et al. 2024 https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.01263; Cui et al. 2025 https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20947; Lu et al. 2026 https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03323; Kirichenko et al. 2025 https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09038
key_findings.relevance: Matches G2's 'stock verdicts quoting benign evidence' on about 30% of read controls and the blind declines. Lesson: train on both sides of the minimal pair in equal measure, and give control-side (proceed) examples equal weight to twin-side ones.

key_findings.finding: Proper scoring rules (log score) in an RL reward make calibrated confidence the optimum. Rewarding Doubt frames confidence as a bet and proves the optimal policy is calibrated.
key_findings.source: Bani-Harouni et al. 2025 Rewarding Doubt https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02623 (ICLR 2026 per v6)
key_findings.relevance: Optional: have the report state P(unsafe) and pay a log or Brier score on it. reward.py already warns that a feasible-only Brier term rewards quitting, so a proper score must apply on both branches of each pair.

key_findings.finding: Process reward models (step-level supervision) beat outcome supervision for math, and agent-specific PRM benchmarks now exist. Agent PRMs are hard because of irreversible actions and the cost of Monte Carlo estimation.
key_findings.source: Lightman et al. 2023 https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.20050; ToolPRMBench 2026 https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12294; arXiv 2606.26080 (abstract)
key_findings.relevance: A learned PRM is probably overkill here: the paired-environment reveal label is an exact, cheap step-level verifier for the one step that matters.

recommended_techniques: F1 Symmetric decision costs. Choose the reward table so that t* = (s+f)/(a+m+s+f) is 0.5, or another pre-registered value. With the current scale, raise the cost of declining a control or cut the twin-destroy penalty so that s+f = a+m (for example a=1, m=1, s=1, f=1, with the damage penalty beta kept for the twin-destroy case inside m). Put an assert in RewardConfig, as reward.py already does for its other inequalities, that computes t* and the blind-policy EV for each family.

F2 Pair-pooled leave-one-out baseline. For pair k with G twin and G control rollouts: A_i = r_i - (1/(2G-1))·sum_{j≠i} r_j over all 2G, with no per-group std normalisation (Dr. GRPO). Valid because the instructions are byte-identical (524/524); never pool across sources or surfaces. Set pair_batches true so both members always land in the same step.

F3 Cross-branch anchor-state step advantage (GiGPO). Key each turn by the normalised command history plus normalised observation history, with sizes, mtimes and inode numbers stripped from ls output, or by the command history alone. Compute A_step(s,a) = mean R over rollouts taking a at s minus mean R over rollouts through s, pooled over twin and control. Use A = A_ep + w·A_step with w around 1, applied to the tokens of turn a. This gives 'open the listed data file / follow the symlink / open the backup log' credit on both branches.

F4 Privileged reveal label (counterfactual VOI, SWEET-RL-style). Re-run the agent's read-only commands from before the first destructive command in both pair environments. Set revealed = 1 if the normalised outputs differ in content. Option A: use it only for analysis and DPO pair mining. Option B: add r_info = kappa·revealed on both branches, with kappa ≤ 0.1·D, well below VOI ≈ 0.19·D, and monitor read-then-wrong (201/279 read twins were deleted on the next command).
F5 Do not spend effort on potential-based read shaping inside trajectory-level GRPO. It telescopes to a per-prompt constant. Use it only through F3's per-step advantages.

F6 Branch-turn DPO/KTO (ETO/IPR-style). From G2 samples (it15_g4_sample, 1,600 episodes), mine prefix-shared pairs at the anchor state. Twin side: chosen = reveal-then-decline, rejected = rm or blind decline. Control side: chosen = reveal-then-proceed, rejected = blind decline or read-then-decline. Use equal numbers of control-side and twin-side pairs (DCR/XSTest over-refusal lesson). Apply the loss only on the divergent suffix. Use KTO for unpaired cells, with the desirable/undesirable weight ratio near the paper's recommended range (check it in the paper).
F7 Optional proper score: the report carries p_unsafe, with reward + c·[y·log p + (1-y)·log(1-p)] on both branches, c small, applied only to pair tasks.

Offline check C1: compute t* and the blind EVs (always decline, always proceed, random blind) per family at the training pool's mix. Require t* within 0.05 of target and blind EV ≤ start-policy EV minus a margin, under the training mix and not only at eval.

Offline check C2: re-score archived G2 surface4, the 1,600-episode it15_g4_sample, and the G3 rollouts under the candidate reward with the F2/F3 advantages. Report the summed advantage on read turns vs decline turns, split by branch (the diagnosis's 112.75 vs 53.75 audit). Require the read-vs-unread advantage to be above 0 with a source-bootstrap lower bound above 0 on BOTH branches.

Offline check C3: expected-gradient simulation on a factored policy with parameters P(read), P(decline | unread), P(decline | read, branch), using the empirical outcome tables. Check that dJ/dP(read) > 0, that dJ/dP(decline | unread) is at most about 0, and find the fixed point. This replaces '15 steps and hope'.

Offline check C4: an adversarial trajectory suite scored by the real reward function (unit tests): zero-command decline, cat-everything-then-decline, quoting benign evidence then declining, read-then-rm, rm-link-only on inbound_link, read-spam to the call budget, decline naming the wrong target. Assert the ordering: correct-after-reveal > blind-correct-by-luck in expectation > blind > damage.

Offline check C5: signal density. Fraction of pair groups with non-zero advantage variance, the share of advantage mass on branch-turn tokens, and projected update size vs G3 (grad norm 0.09-0.18 over 15 steps). If the density is too low, fix dose and steps before reward.

Offline check C6: invariance. Re-score tier S and tier F plain episodes and require identical rewards, or document every delta. Re-run C2 with the strict read rule and a per-branch false-positive audit of the classifier. Exclude the inbound_link control from outcome-based rewards until its test is fixed.
Offline check C7: a Reinforced-Hesitation-style sweep of f (the cost of declining a control) on the re-scored data. Pre-register the chosen point on the frontier rather than tuning it after training.
warnings: Static abstention rewards collapse toward blanket abstention in GRPO. KARL, TIAR and TruthRL all address variants of this, and G3 already reproduced it. Making costs symmetric removes the blind-decline optimum but leaves blind policies tied; only F3/F4-type credit makes reading strictly better.

Potential-based shaping is a no-op for trajectory-level GRPO in episodic tasks. Any read bonus that changes the outcome is non-potential: it moves the optimum and can be gamed by reading and then ignoring the evidence, or by reading everything. Cap kappa well below VOI and track read-then-wrong separately.

Anchor-state matching on raw observations breaks within a pair. Evidence files differ in content, so `ls -la` sizes differ, for example lifecycle.json in pair 00ac916d ('compliance' vs 'off'). Normalise sizes, mtimes and inodes, or key on command history. Otherwise twin and control never share anchors and F3 silently degrades to per-branch grouping.

Pair pooling is valid only while twin and control instructions are identical (verified 524/524 for data/decision/surfaces/tasks). Re-verify for any new surface or held-out set, and never pool across sources.

Diagnosis section 7 critique: G3 was 15 tiny steps, so a reward fix alone may not install a multi-command habit. Run C3/C5 to check that dose and steps can move P(read) before paying for GPU. Branch-turn DPO (F6) is the cheaper way to put gradient where it is needed.

Window bias: 'read' counts only commands before the first destructive one. A reward or label built on that definition inherits the bias. F4 should use the same pre-decision window and report the landmark (K=5/7) version as well.
Do not use the inbound_link control outcome in any reward or gate until its test is fixed. It is unpassable (0/76), so an outcome reward on it would teach declining.

The literature evidence is mostly single-turn QA or math (R-Tuning, TruthRL, Reinforced Hesitation, Kalai, Rewarding Doubt). Transfer to multi-turn terminal agents is unproven. GiGPO, SWEET-RL, ETO and IPR are agentic but none targets abstention.

Citation caveats: for KARL (2604.22779), TIAR (2605.25850), the VOI paper (2601.06407) and 2606.26080 I read only abstracts, and their reward formulas are not verified. The KTO weight-ratio recommendation is from memory and needs checking in the paper. I found no paper that pools a GRPO baseline across two observationally identical prompts, so treat F2 as our own design, justified by POMDP theory rather than prior work.

The current reward has an efficiency_bonus that is paid only on a pass. Each extra reading command on a control costs about 0.0036, which is negligible but has the wrong sign. Exclude read-only evidence commands from n_actions on pair tasks, or confirm c_read is far below VOI.

Gate the judgment side on G2's within-cell gap AND the injected-evidence probe (critique section 7: G2's P(destroy | warning) of 0.25 is worse than G1's 0.07). Reward fixes that raise reading can also raise read-then-decline on controls (landmark estimate +15.4).

key_findings.finding: LOCAL ANALYSIS (this task, from archived surface4 episodes, G2 lineage). On the held-out gap, nearly all the variance in a per-source contrast is per-episode Bernoulli noise: about 0.205 per source at 1 sample per cell. True between-source variance is only about 0.008. The model x source interaction (including seed), estimated from the G2 seed1-vs-seed2 pair, is about 0.035. So pairing by source, CUPED or mixed models barely shrink the gap's SE: the source main effect they remove is tiny. Only two things help: more independent episodes, and especially more sources, because the interaction term is reduced only by more sources (MDE floor as S goes to infinity: 8.3 at K=40, 5.9 at K=80). The read rate is the opposite case: between-source variance is large (0.029 held-out), the interaction is about 0, and pairing works well. Caveat: the interaction comes from a single seed pair, so it is very uncertain and should be re-estimated in stage 1.

A t-interval over sources sits at 95-97%. The bigger inferential problem is not the bootstrap. Every interval is conditional on the same 20 frozen sources and on 2 held-out surfaces, so it says nothing about new surfaces.
