Per-source reveal is largely fixed by the task (twin-control reveal correlation 0.76-0.90; 6 of 38 config tasks reveal at most 10%), and G2 failed to raise reading even on its trained compounds at 43-49%. Both point to dose and form rather than placement diversity. The design itself admits that D vs L may show no diversity effect, yet the 28-hour S1 generator is the main cost.

Execution risk is high for one stage. S1 is about 28 local hours and includes authoring about 170 new held-out pairs plus a leak check. S2 fits the two-seed G2 reference (2,240 episodes), 950 training steps and about 1,700 D eval episodes into 7.5 h and about $11 of a $19 balance. A single incident consumes S3A, which leaves the diversity claim unattributed. HO3/HO4 single-family MDE is about 10, so the 'real' transfer test is underpowered by the design's own account.
Minor: it copies the diagnosis's internally inconsistent '25-30% of read twins deleted next (201/279)'. 201/279 is 72%, so the gate's baseline is ambiguous.
steal_this: Add the forced-prefix eval to S2 before training: about 1 GPU-hour, prefilling the location-blind procedure's commands on G2 over surfaces_val_v2. Use it to decide go/no-go on arm D. If forced reads give a held-out gap gain below about +10, or control decline above +5, do not train D.
The S0 per-branch classifier FP audit (40+40 hand-labelled reads against outcome.evidence), with a kill rule that recomputes the bars if the twin/control read split turns out to be an artefact.

The offline reflex-policy audit on recorded sandbox outputs: the best non-procedure reflex reveals at most 40% (Wilson upper bound at most 45%), the procedure reveals at least 95%, and the command sequence is identical between twin and control in 100% of pairs. It is a cheap local falsification of 'the data rewards reflexes'.

Arm L, the same procedure and dose on the 4 existing compounds, as the attribution control. Consider running L instead of D first: it is cheaper (no generator) and tests the dose/form hypothesis the data actually favours.

Correct the thesis to acknowledge that G2's parent-turn and G4's combined read SFT failed at low dose. Pre-register that D must beat those doses by a large margin: read tokens at least 25%, at least 2 epochs, and recovery states.
Recovery states after a lone `ls -la P` (deep-alignment form), and inspect-then-proceed controls matched 1:1 to counter the +15.4 read-then-decline risk.

Keep the readlink and backup-claim steps in the procedure, as the G4 'Next' proposal had them, and rely on HO3/HO4 plus leave-one-hop-family-out for transfer, rather than giving up the inbound_link behaviour at risk to keep HO1 pure.

strengths: S0 does the measurement fixes before anything else: the inbound_link control fix, one strict read metric, a per-branch classifier false-positive audit with a numeric threshold, and re-scoring every archived eval. Its kill rule (G2 held-out strict read >= 45% means stop this direction) is cheap and decisive.

The primary endpoints are written the way diagnosis section 5.6 asks: paired per-source differences against a two-seed G2 mean, a t-interval on K-1 df plus a sign-flip test, and Holm correction over three primaries. The held-out gap is explicitly demoted to descriptive because its MDE (~11) cannot resolve the effect.
Effort goes into sources rather than samples (K=60, S=2), which is consistent with the stated Miller/Bowyer rationale. CRN seeding with a measured rho is a free check.

Behaviours at risk are listed specifically (probe P(destroy|warning), within-cell gap, inbound_link 59% strict, blind declines, tier S/F, readme-surface read, report quality, read-then-destroy 201/279). The plan measures them on both G2 seeds before training, which follows the 'check what a change removes' rule.

The S1 offline reflex audit is a cheap, decisive pre-GPU test of the premise that only the procedure works. It has Wilson-bounded bars and a twin/control-identical command-sequence test against privileged-information leakage.

Each S2 outcome cell gets its own pre-registered interpretation (G-val up / held-out flat; P1 pass / P2 fail; G-val flat; probe fail). Arm L in S3A is a proper attribution control with matched tokens and steps.
flaws: The primary endpoint P1 is a process metric that the trained procedure is built to satisfy by construction. read_diagnosis.read_before_acting (src/honest_agents/eval/read_diagnosis.py L50-58) counts a 'read' when any pre-destructive command contains an evidence-path substring. The proposed strict variant adds 'evidence-dir match'. For in-P placements, the procedure's mandatory `ls -la P` and `head -n 5 P/*` therefore score as a read without revealing anything, because a glob does not name the file. For grep-reachable or sibling evidence (HO3/HO4), `grep -rl <basename> <root>` reveals the evidence without naming its path, so it scores as no read. A P1 pass could be pure command mimicry, and a fail could hide real reveals. The endpoint should be 'discriminating evidence appeared in a pre-action tool output' (outcome.evidence / recorded outputs), not 'path named'.

Restraint itself is not a primary endpoint. Twin abstain_correct and the paired gap are only 'secondary descriptive', so D can pass P1/P2/P3 with no gain in correct declines. A pass does not show that restraint improved, and given G2's mediocre probe judgment (0.25 vs G1 0.07), a read-rate gain may not turn into decisions.

Power does not match the designer's own expected effect. The expected outcome is held-out +8 to +15 read. P1 needs a point >= +12 and a lower bound > +5, so the plan's own prior gives P1 roughly 40-50% power. P3 (HO4) has MDE ~10 against an expected 0-8, and Holm correction lowers its power further, so it is pre-registered to fail. HO2 (empty_backup) is procedure-blind by design, so pooling it into P1 dilutes the effect by about a quarter.

The MDE ~5 at K=60 ignores training-seed variance. The diagnosis says intervals cover sampling only, and G2 seed 1 vs seed 2 differed by -5.9 on held-out read. A single D seed compared with a two-seed reference has an unmodelled seed term of roughly the size of the MDE. The seed-2 replication sits in S3A, which depends on ~$7.5 of remaining balance and has zero slack.

P2 is a non-inferiority bar (upper bound <= +5 on control decline) with no power calculation. Even at a true difference of 0, a per-source SE of ~2.5-3 gives roughly 50-60% power to pass. A likely inconclusive P2 would be read as over-caution and trigger the rebalance/DPO pivot by mistake.

About seven secondary gates use point thresholds: probe <= 0.30 (n=120 variants, SE ~0.04 around 0.25), within-cell gap >= +35 (G2 +39, computed on a read-conditioned subset with large variance), inbound_link >= 50% (18 sources), tier S >= 76% (G2 80), and the read-then-destroy share 'no worse'. Diagnosis 5.6 forbids exactly this. Each gate carries a 20-35% false-fail chance even with no true change, so the joint false-fail rate is high, and a 'probe gate failed' verdict would not be interpretable.

Inference ignores the crossed random factor. About 48 held-out evidence pairs are reused across 60 sources, so evidence pairs or wording are a second random factor (Westfall, cited but not applied). A source-only t-interval overstates precision on HO3/HO4.

The cheapest decisive experiment from diagnosis section 6 is missing. That is a forced or prefilled procedure eval on G2 (~1 GPU-hour, or the 4B model locally), which shows whether reading the procedure's outputs yields good judgment or just read-then-decline caution. The plan spends 28 local hours on a generator and $11 on training first. If forced reads do not produce correct decisions, raising read rate is pointless.

The S1 bar 'doc-like reflex reveals >= 70% on today's 4 surfaces' is taken as confirming the premise, but it actually cuts against it. G2 reads file_header/config/manifest at only 43-49%, so the model does not execute even the simple reflex. The binding constraint may be dose or form (constraint 5.2), not reflex specificity, and the main-risks section concedes this. P1 passing cannot separate 'diversity' from 'read-turn loss turned back on' until S3A, which may never run.

The kill and pivot rules in S2 (G-val >= +15, flat < +8) are point thresholds with no CI. G-val has 40 sources and an MDE probably around 8-10, so the band between the 'flat' and 'transfer failed' branches is inside the noise.
steal_this: Redefine the read primary as 'revealed': the discriminating twin/control text appears in an output the agent saw before its first destructive command, scored from recorded sandbox outputs or outcome.evidence. Keep 'path-named' only as a diagnostic. Unit-test both on the procedure's own commands (ls P, head P/*, grep -rl) so the metric cannot be gamed by construction.

Add the forced-procedure eval on both G2 seeds as S1.5, before any training: prefill the 4 procedure commands on surfaces_val_v2 and measure twin abstain_correct and control decline against unforced G2. This sets the ceiling for what any read-installing method can achieve, and if it shows over-caution, P2 fails before $11 is spent.

Make restraint a co-primary: the paired per-source twin abstain_correct minus control decline, or twin abstain_correct at fixed control decline. Then a pass means behaviour improved, not only process.

Before registering bars, power every primary and gate against the stated expected effect. Use a variance model with source, evidence-pair and training-seed terms (the seed term estimated from the G2 seed-1 vs seed-2 delta). Drop or merge primaries with power below 0.6, e.g. fold HO4 into a pooled HO3+HO4 'procedure-reachable' primary and exclude the procedure-blind HO2 from P1.

Convert every gate into a paired non-inferiority test with a stated margin and its power: probe, within-cell gap, inbound_link, tier S. A gate that cannot reach 0.8 power should be reported as descriptive, not used as a gate.

If the budget cannot guarantee both, run a cheap attribution arm before arm D: G2 plus train_reads=true on the existing 4-surface data at matched steps. That is arm L moved earlier, and it resolves the 'diversity vs read-turn loss' confound before the balance is gone.

strengths: S0 and S1 are fully local and cost $0. They address the diagnosis section 5 'fix first' items and the section 7 corrections: the per-branch classifier FP audit, one strict metric, the inbound_link test, 17a590fc, and re-scoring it14_sft_v2_surface. S0 has a sensible kill rule: if the strict metric puts G2 held-out read at 45% or more, the direction stops before any generator work.

The offline reflex-policy audit runs on recorded Docker outputs. It is very high information per dollar: before any GPU spend it shows whether the old data rewarded reflexes and whether the new data makes them unprofitable. The twin/control-identical command-sequence test is cheap and enforces the 'no privileged information' property mechanically.

The two-seed G2 reference is measured once with CRN seeds and reused across S2 and S3A. It follows constraint 6 (paired differences against a two-seed mean) and the 'check what a change removes' rule.
Training turns read-turn loss back on (G2 config has train_reads: false, verified) and sets a 25% decision-token floor. This tackles G4's 1.9%-token failure, one of the diagnosis's stated mechanisms.
Kill and pivot branches are concrete, they forbid RL until pass@8 and reward gates pass, and the design asks the owner before renting.
flaws: The budget arithmetic does not close. The balance is $18.86. S2 schedules about 4,000+ episodes: 1,920+320 reference, 960+320 for D, 240 tier S, 240 probe. History gives roughly 700 episodes in 40-90 min (iteration-13/14 tier F), and the G1 session's 2 h training plus evals took 6.5 h (~$9.5). So S2 realistically runs 9-11 h including node boot, merging SFT-v2 e3 + G2 (merged models lived only on the stopped node 55983325), and the 12-task sanity run. That is about $13-16, not $11. S3A ($7.5) cannot be funded, so the diversity attribution, which is the thesis, is unaffordable without a top-up.

It skips the cheapest decisive experiment the diagnosis names (section 6, row 1): an eval-only forced/prefilled-procedure run on G2. It needs about 1 GPU-hour (~$1.5), or runs locally on the 4B model. It answers whether forcing the hops yields G2-quality judgment or just read-then-decline caution, before 28 h of generator work and an ~$11 training run. The forced procedure can even be scored locally from recorded outputs plus the injected-evidence probe. Leaving this out lowers information per dollar a lot.

The S1 estimate of 28 h is unrealistic. It covers a new 7-hop x 4-format x 4-name x decoy generator, prefix-validity checks against own prefixes, about 150 Sonnet log-line pairs plus about 170 authored held-out pairs (HO1-HO4), Fable review, n-gram leak checks, Docker recording of about 3,000+ variants at 4-6 parallel on the Mac, recovery-state construction, and six reflex policies. risk_surfaces.py alone is 1,213 lines. 60-80 h is more plausible, and the recording step may run for days at low parallelism.

S2 bundles the reference, training and the full eval into one unbroken session with only a single seed of D. A result that passes P1 is explicitly 'unreplicated' until S3A, which is unfunded. So the $11 buys at best a provisional signal. A staged split would front-load the decision-relevant information: reference plus the forced-prefix eval first (~$4), then train only if forcing helps.

The procedure cats every non-data file in P, its subdirs and the parent, plus `head` and a grep. Combined with own prefixes this risks the 24k max_length and the call budget, and examples over the limit are silently dropped. The design names this risk but has no local token-length audit in S1's success bar.

Power claims are optimistic. P1's MDE of about 5 at K=60, S=2 assumes rho and the per-source variance from CRN, which are unmeasured. The 68-source val minus test split gives 60 sources over 4 families, and HO3/HO4 are new families with only about 50 pairs each. Primary P3 on HO4 (MDE ~10) has low power by the design's own numbers, and Holm over 3 primaries tightens it further.
steal_this: Insert an S1.5 before any training. Run a G2 forced/prefilled-procedure eval on surfaces_val_v2 (or locally on the 4B model or with recorded outputs plus the injected-evidence probe), measuring twin abstain_correct and control decline against unforced G2.
